# Role recipe (v1)

Schema for `.tera/roles/<name>.hcl` recipes per ADR-060 §1. A role is a named bundle of `grant` and `deny` blocks, each in the ADR-010 vocabulary (actions + hierarchical resource patterns). Roles compile deterministically to an ordered ACL ruleset enforced by the unchanged ADR-010 ACLAuthorizer; a `role_binding` maps subjects to roles. The recipe declares a single `role` block whose label becomes `name`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `recipe/role` |
| Regime | persisted |
| Identity regime | `recipe` — the filename stem is the identity; the file declares exactly one resource, and a block label — where the grammar admits one — must equal the stem (ADR-087 D3) |
| Current version | `v1` |
| Supported versions | `v1` |
| Schema `$id` | `https://kottera.dev/schemas/recipe/role/v1` |
| Go source | `github.com/kottera/kottera/pkg/systemvault/schemas.roleRecipe` |
| Served at | `GET /api/v1/schemas/recipe/role/{version}` |
| JSON Schema | `GET /api/v1/schemas/recipe/role/v1` |

## Example

A minimal `role`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/roles/example-role.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

role "example-role" {
  grant {
    actions   = ["invoke"]
    resources = ["api/v1/workorders/list"]
  }
}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | yes | — | — | const `v1` | Per-recipe grammar version. Required; this schema applies when version is v1. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | — | min length 1 | Bare role name (the HCL block label). The loader namespaces it as <vault-id>/roles/<name>. |
| `grant` | block (list) | no | — | — | — | Allow grants. Each entry authorizes the listed actions over the listed resource patterns for any subject bound to this role. |
| `deny` | block (list) | no | — | — | — | Deny grants. ADR-060 §1 deny-overrides: every deny from any role a subject holds compiles ahead of every allow. |

## `grant` block

Repeatable.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `actions` | string[] | yes | — | — | min items 1; items one of `connect`, `publish`, `subscribe`, `invoke`, `*` | ADR-010 actions. * expands to the full set (connect, publish, subscribe, invoke). This vocabulary is CLOSED and the loader enforces it: a token outside the list is refused when the recipe loads, naming the token, the file and the valid set. It used to be dropped in silence, so a grant naming only a misspelling compiled to an empty action list — a role that granted nothing, from a recipe that loaded clean. A misspelling beside a valid token is refused for the same reason rather than narrowed to the tokens that parsed. |
| `resources` | string[] | yes | — | — | min items 1; items min length 1 | Hierarchical resource patterns (ADR-010): tools/#, api/v1/config/apply, extensions/authenticator/#, topic patterns, etc. |
| `scope` | string | no | — | — | — | Reserved tenancy namespace (ADR-060 §7). Defaults to the single global scope in v1; carries no behaviour yet. |
